documentation: Every corvidae workspace's disposition when the mirror transform emits a public target, plus a ruling on each name that is published (or was once reserved) without corvidae source. The transform hard-errors on any workspace absent from `workspaces`; it never silently skips one. `publish-as` carries the public npm name, and is the only disposition that puts anything on the registry. `private-workspace` ships to the mirror repository but never into a tarball. `exclude` is not emitted at all. Names under `publishedOnly` have no corvidae source, so no sync can maintain them: `keep` means a human maintains it elsewhere, `deprecate` means publish a deprecation notice, and `orphan-untouched` means leave the registry entry exactly as it is.

@lostgradient/telephone.reason: Never published and new in this repository. It carries an Operative agent run onto the chat stream wire, and its only consumer is `@lostgradient/desktop`, which the owner excluded from the mirror — so nothing the mirror emits depends on it. `private-workspace` would ship its source to the public repository, making a brand-new package public for the first time as a side effect of an internal refactor; `exclude` keeps that a deliberate decision. Reversible: promote to `private-workspace` or `publish-as` when a public consumer exists.

@lostgradient/weft.name: @lostgradient/weft
@lostgradient/weft.reason: Already published under this name. Ships standalone from stevekinney/weft.

@lostgradient/weft-ui.name: @lostgradient/weft-ui
@lostgradient/weft-ui.reason: Name is settled, but `npm view @lostgradient/weft-ui` returns 404 — the manifest carries 0.1.0 and no `private` flag, yet it was never published. COR-1194 records that its trusted-publisher registration was never completed. Treat the first monorepo release as a first publish, not a re-publish.

@lostgradient/cinder.name: @lostgradient/cinder
@lostgradient/cinder.reason: Already published under this name. Its exports map is regenerated by the transform per COR-1186, not copied.

armorer.name: armorer
armorer.reason: Keeps its unscoped name deliberately. Roughly 30,872 installs a month; renaming breaks real consumers for a cosmetic gain.

conversationalist.name: conversationalist
conversationalist.reason: Keeps its unscoped name deliberately. Roughly 53,608 installs a month, the most-installed package in the graph.

@lostgradient/cryptography.name: @lostgradient/cryptography
@lostgradient/cryptography.reason: Inside the runtime dependency closure of published armorer and operative, so it must publish or those packages are uninstallable. Never published before. The unscoped name `cryptography` belongs to an unrelated third party (jnssnmrcs, 1.2.3, 2018) and is unavailable. Scoped name approved by the repository owner 2026-09-18.

@lostgradient/embeddings.name: @lostgradient/embeddings
@lostgradient/embeddings.reason: Inside the runtime dependency closure of published armorer and operative. Never published before. The unscoped name `embeddings` belongs to an unrelated third party (pagepixels, 2.0.5, 2023) and is unavailable. Scoped name approved by the repository owner 2026-09-18.

@lostgradient/tool-protocol.name: @lostgradient/tool-protocol
@lostgradient/tool-protocol.reason: Inside the runtime dependency closure of four published packages. Never published before. The unscoped name `tool-protocol` is genuinely unregistered, but the scoped name was chosen for consistency with its siblings and approved by the repository owner 2026-09-18.

@lostgradient/lifecycle.name: @lostgradient/lifecycle
@lostgradient/lifecycle.reason: Inside the runtime dependency closure of four published packages, reached both directly and through tool-protocol. Never published — agent-bureau's manifest is `private: true` at 0.0.1. The unscoped name `lifecycle` belongs to an unrelated third party (kmalakoff, 1.0.4, 2015) and is unavailable. Scoped name approved by the repository owner 2026-09-18.

@lostgradient/typescript.reason: Every published package extends it, but only through devDependencies — it appears in no runtime `dependencies` edge anywhere. Must remain in the repository because dropping it breaks typecheck and build for every workspace. COR-1189 vendors it to a local path for the single-package weft target and keeps it workspace-native for the monorepo.

@lostgradient/testing.reason: Test infrastructure imported from 505 test files and 26 non-test files, all of which are harnesses, fixture loaders, and scripts. Never in a runtime dependencies edge. COR-1196 states this disposition explicitly: it ships to the mirror repository but never into a tarball.

@lostgradient/desktop.reason: The application formerly named `chat-room`, which the repository owner excluded from the mirror on 2026-09-21 because it is not part of the mirror tooling and `private-workspace` would ship its source to the public cinder repository beside the lab already living there at `labs/chat-room`. Replacing the SvelteKit lab with an Electrobun desktop application changes the implementation, not that reasoning, so the exclusion carries over rather than reverting to `private-workspace`. No workspace declares it as a dependency. Reversible: promote to `private-workspace` and rule on its layout if it should ever become public.

@lostgradient/bureau.reason: Excluded from the mirror by the repository owner, 2026-09-19. Never published and never public: agent-bureau's manifest is `private: true`, and the identically-named public npm package belongs to an unrelated third party. `private-workspace` would still ship the source to the public mirror repository, which would make it public for the first time; `exclude` keeps it in corvidae only. Nothing outside the bureau/memory/skills cluster depends on it, so excluding all three breaks no other workspace. Reversible: promote to `publish-as` or `private-workspace` if it should become public later.

publishedOnly.policy: Names with no corvidae source. A sync can never maintain these, so each needs an explicit ruling rather than silence. `deprecate` is permanently public and requires the repository owner's approval; none is currently set.

entries.reason: Public with provenance, but it has no corvidae source, so no sync can maintain it. Leaving the registry entry exactly as it is breaks no consumer, whereas deprecating it is a permanently public act. Revisit deliberately rather than as a migration side effect.

openQuestions: @lostgradient/bureau, @lostgradient/memory and @lostgradient/skills are excluded from the mirror entirely, ruled by the repository owner 2026-09-19 once it was clear that `private-workspace` still ships source to the public mirror repository. They stay in corvidae. Each has an available @lostgradient/* name if that changes.

@lostgradient/cinder-mcp is left untouched rather than deprecated. It has no corvidae source and therefore no maintenance path through this pipeline; whether it should be deprecated, re-homed, or given source is unresolved.

COR-1189's surface-parity gate fetches each published package's last subpath set from the registry. The four packages newly marked publish-as here have no published predecessor, so that gate has no baseline for them and must treat a missing predecessor as a first publish rather than a parity failure.
